# StockSaathi

> StockSaathi (also written Stock Saathi) is a free stock market simulator and paper trading app for Indian teenagers aged 13 to 18. Users practise investing with ₹1,00,000 of virtual money on real NSE and BSE stocks, ETFs and mutual funds at real market prices, and an AI coach flags beginner mistakes, such as panic-selling and FOMO buying, as they make them. It is built for complete beginners, uses no real money, and is not a broker or investment adviser.

StockSaathi teaches by doing rather than through lessons: there are no course modules or quizzes. Learning comes from placing practice trades, being coached on your own decisions, replaying real Indian market crashes, and reviewing a report card that grades decision quality.

## Key facts

- Price: free. No paid plan, no subscription, no in-app purchases; it never asks for payment details.
- Audience: Indian teens aged 13–18, including complete beginners, school and college students. Anyone 13 or older can sign up.
- Money: ₹1,00,000 of virtual money per account. Nothing can be deposited, withdrawn or converted into anything real. No real shares are bought or sold.
- Markets: 4,000+ stocks listed on the NSE and BSE (including NSE SME listings), 300+ ETFs and 8,000+ active mutual fund schemes, at real market prices. Prices can be delayed; it is not a live trading feed. No futures and options, crypto or foreign stocks.
- Orders: market orders, limit orders and after-market orders (AMOs). Pending orders are filled on the server even when the app is closed.
- AI coach ("Saathi"): checks every trade for nine common mistakes — panic-selling, FOMO buying, pump-chasing, anchoring to 52-week highs or lows, single-stock concentration, sector concentration, the disposition effect, churning and overtrading — and explains what it noticed in the user's own numbers. It answers finance questions in English, or in Hinglish when Hinglish mode is switched on in Settings. It never recommends buying or selling a security and does not predict prices.
- Panic-sell intervention: before a likely panic-sell, the app pauses and shows how long similar past dips took to recover (measured from real daily prices since 2011, for that stock or the Nifty 50), then lets the user decide.
- Crash replays ("Time Travel"): day-by-day replays of the COVID-19 crash (2020), the 2008 global financial crisis and the 2016 demonetisation shock, built from real daily Nifty 50 closes, comparing a ₹1,00,000 portfolio that held with one that sold everything on day three and stayed in cash. Results: in the COVID-19 replay (19 Feb to 9 Nov 2020) holding finished 5.6% ahead; in the 2008 replay (8 Jan to 27 Oct 2008) selling early won, because the Nifty fell 60%; in the demonetisation replay (8 Nov 2016 to 28 Feb 2017) holding finished 7.0% ahead. Featured AI-built replays cover the Harshad Mehta scam (1992), the dot-com crash (2000), Satyam (2009), IL&FS (2018), DHFL (2019), YES Bank (2020), the Paytm IPO (2021) and the Adani–Hindenburg report (2023); users can generate replays of other events.
- Report card: a letter grade from A+ to D that updates after every decision and weighs behaviour more than returns, with badges for habits like diversifying and holding long term.
- What it is not: StockSaathi at stocksaathi.co.in never sells subscriptions, stock tips, trading signals or trading bots. Unrelated products use similar names.
- Real investing for under-18s: in India a minor cannot open a trading account independently; a guardian can open and operate a demat account in the minor's name. StockSaathi needs no demat account, broker or money.
- Social: users can send virtual cash to friends by @username or redeem code. There is deliberately no leaderboard ranking users by returns.
- News: Indian market headlines from major business news sources, tagged bullish, bearish or neutral.
- Without an account, visitors can browse markets and charts, read news, chat with the AI coach and play the curated crash replays. Trading and keeping a portfolio need a free account.
- Compliance: StockSaathi is an educational simulator. It is not a SEBI-registered broker, investment adviser or research analyst, and is not affiliated with SEBI, NSE or BSE. Any account and its data can be deleted on request via grievance@stocksaathi.co.in.

## Pages

- [Home](https://stocksaathi.co.in/): what StockSaathi is, with an FAQ.
- [Markets](https://stocksaathi.co.in/stocks): 4,000+ NSE and BSE stocks, ETFs and mutual funds; stock pages by sector.
- [Crash replays](https://stocksaathi.co.in/crash-replay): replay real Indian market crashes.
- [COVID-19 crash replay (2020)](https://stocksaathi.co.in/crash-replay/COVID_2020)
- [Global financial crisis replay (2008)](https://stocksaathi.co.in/crash-replay/GFC_2008)
- [Demonetisation replay (2016)](https://stocksaathi.co.in/crash-replay/DEMO_2016)
- [AI coach](https://stocksaathi.co.in/chat): ask Saathi about investing and Indian markets.
- [Learn the stock market](https://stocksaathi.co.in/learn-stock-market): a beginner's guide for Indian teens.
- [For students, parents and teachers](https://stocksaathi.co.in/for-students)
- [Privacy policy](https://stocksaathi.co.in/privacy), [Terms of use](https://stocksaathi.co.in/terms), [Grievance officer](https://stocksaathi.co.in/grievance)

Individual stock pages (with each stock's real dip-recovery history since 2011) follow the pattern https://stocksaathi.co.in/stocks/SYMBOL (for example https://stocksaathi.co.in/stocks/RELIANCE).
